newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open higher as Dow rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open higher as Dow rebounds.

text.p: Australian shares opened higher on Wednesday after the Dow's turnaround and as gold stocks stemmed the bleeding of recent days.
The All Ordinaries index was up 16.8 points at 2,417.5 in early trading.

After clinging to support at the 2,400 level on Tuesday, solid local support emerged after Wall Street reversed its early losses. Meanwhile, the gold index showed its first positive move of 1997 after the bullion price steadied in offshore markets.
"Bonds have steadied and metals prices were a little better as well," said Greg Matthews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual Investment Management.
He said he saw the local market as attractive value and expected further increases.

"It is still cheap relative to cash and bonds. It had the wobbles over the last couple of days after it reached those fresh highs, but having digested the December moves, we are looking for it to move up through January," Matthews said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
